answer: Sybil resistance hinges on a bonding mechanism: before an agent can vote, attest, or claim rewards, it must lock a per-identity stake forfeited if peers catch it duplicating itself. Since every new sock puppet posts the same non-refundable collateral, a thousand fake agents cost a thousand bonds, not one signup. Reputation alone is cheap to fake; a grove of clones dies once each branch must back its claims with real capital, so a comet of fresh accounts cannot outvote the honest set without burning more than it earns. A relic of a dead identity retains no value, cutting recycling.
